title: Beef Tartare with Tomato Sabayon & Chips

ingredientSections.heading: Steak Tartare
items: 300g high-quality lean and freshly ground beef

methodSections.heading: Tomato Sabayon
steps: In a small saucepan, bring the white wine and vinegar to a boil. Reduce mixture by half and cool to room temperature. In a separate, non-stick pan, brown the tomato paste over medium low heat.
Over a double boiler, combine the cooled wine reduction and the egg yolks in a large bowl and whisk constantly until the mixture thickens.
Remove from heat and very slowly add the oil while continually whisking. If you add the oil too quickly, the sauce will break and you'll need to start over.
Add the roasted tomato paste and adjust the consistency with water. Season to taste.

methodSections.heading: Chips
steps: Wash and cut the potatoes in half lengthwise but leave the skin on. Slice into 1-2mm thick slices with a mandoline or a very sharp knife. Place the potato slices into a large bowl of cold water as you slice.
Drain the bowl and rinse the sliced potato until the water runs clear. Fill the bowl with fresh water, add the salt and soak the potatoes for at least 30 minutes.
Heat frying oil in a deep-fryer or large saucepan to 185°C (365°F). Fry potato slices in small batches until nicely coloured and crispy.
Remove from the oil, drain, and season to taste.

methodSections.heading: Steak Tartare
steps: Keep the beef in the fridge. Mince the shallots, capers and chives, and stir through the mustard. Set aside in the fridge.
When the chips are freshly fried and ready to serve, mix the beef and mustard mixture together and season liberally.

Place the tartare mixture on chilled serving plates using a ring mould for a uniform shape. Spoon several dollops of the sabayon on top and arrange the chips in or on the side of the tartare. Serve immediately.
